extracted.intended_audience: prospective Wellcome Trust Investigator Award applicants (researchers and their host institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting a full application for the Wellcome Trust Investigator Awards in Science, covering eligibility, application components (career information, summaries, research vision), host support, budget justification, conflicts, and the review/interview process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility (employment and geographic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be employed in a current academic post with salary covered by the host institution; those imminently taking up a post can apply with a written guarantee of employment. Grant funding calls normally stipulate geographic location of the host organisation (majority of schemes fund the UK, Republic of Ireland and/or low and middle-income economy countries as defined by the OECD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure about eligibility contact Wellcome Trust information officers via the online contact form before starting. Note: Wellcome Trust grants do not cover applicant salaries, only the cost of the research proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and application format (Grant Tracker / full application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be registered on the Wellcome Trust’s Grant Tracker and complete the application entirely online. Investigator Awards require a full grant application to be completed from the outset (a sample PDF is available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are currently multiple schemes (53) with individual eligibility criteria. Investigator Awards are considered three times a year with submission deadlines in March, July, and November—follow scheme-specific instructions closely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant career information and track record
rubrics_metrics.description: The application requests education and career history, the most important research-related career contributions, and up to twenty of the most relevant achievements. Also include peer-reviewed publications, other grants obtained, individuals trained, and research history over the past five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for an exceptional track record in the field relative to career stage. Less experienced/early career candidates should demonstrate an outstanding research record for their stage (e.g., high-impact publications, patents, prior grant funding) and show they are 'on the way to establishing a world-leading reputation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal summaries (expert and lay)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must provide two summaries: one for experts and an additional lay summary that can be easily grasped by lay scientists working in adjacent fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity is key because internal reviewing panels can contain a mix of specialists and non-specialists; explicitly state potential impact. Keep the lay summary accessible to non-specialists in adjacent fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research vision (≤3000 words) — aims, plan, risks, and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a research vision in less than three thousand words outlining the key research questions, why they matter, and a clear plan of how you will achieve them. The outline should be coherent without detailed methodology, and should highlight potential problems and how you will deal with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The research vision should communicate how the project will result in significant advances in the field — reviewers will be looking for ground‑breaking and transformative research. You may add up to 2 A4 pages of figures and data to support your vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support from the host organisation
rubrics_metrics.description: A supporting statement from the host organisation is required describing why the institution thinks you deserve the Investigator Award and how the proposal fits with their aims and priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement should outline how the institute will support you (e.g., ring‑fencing resources, providing financial support, technical assistance) and include information about the applicant's employment contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Details of research group and supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Include details of any research staff who have reported to you over the past two years and anticipated staff to be supervised for the duration of the grant if funded (PhD students, research assistants, postdocs, others even if time is split).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be comprehensive about current and planned team composition and supervisory responsibilities to demonstrate capacity to deliver the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs and budgetary justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed costing for the project with full budgetary justification, separating high‑level costs as headings (examples given: equipment, salaries/stipends, materials and consumables, animals and associated costings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will closely examine this section and will be seeking good value for money in terms of research output versus funding requested — fully justify each resource and its relevance to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest and reviewer suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must declare any potential conflicts of interest arising from the funded research (e.g., consultancies, intellectual property issues). While you cannot formally request peer reviewers, you may suggest who to include or exclude in the 'confidential information' section alongside a brief rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about COIs. Use the confidential information field sparingly and provide clear rationale for reviewer inclusions/exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application assessment: internal and external review and scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission the appropriate internal review group discusses merits and weaknesses and applies a scoring system to rank applications (whether they should definitely go through, are possibly appropriate, or should be rejected). Successful ones proceed to external expert peer-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect structured review stages; reviewers will discuss strengths and weaknesses, and scoring determines who proceeds to external review and interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview preparation and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Shortlisted applicants are invited to an interview requiring a short ten‑minute PowerPoint presentation. Applicants receive anonymised comments from external peer-reviewers in advance to help anticipate questions. Interview panels may include a mix of experts and non-experts from adjacent fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare by conducting mock interviews with research colleagues (especially those successful with grant funding and from adjacent fields). Use anonymised reviewer comments to guide rehearsal and anticipate likely questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborations and joint applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint applicants are welcomed where the collaboration is seen to enhance the scope and quality of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing joint applicants, explain how the collaboration strengthens the research and contributes to the aims; ensure roles and contributions are clear in the application.
